message.content: CXR: Moderate bilateral pleural effusions and mild bibasilar atelectasis; no pulmonary edema. Abnormal rightward cardiac silhouette—cardiomegaly vs pericardial effusion indeterminate. Aorta normal.
Vs prior CXR/CT: Lungs clear, fully expanded. Possible tiny R subpulmonic effusion. Cardiomediastinal/hilar normal. Prior CT: mid-thoracic compression fx + myelomatous infiltration; repeat CT needed.
Pacemaker leads in RA/RV. Stable heart/mediastinum. Basal interstitial opacities unchanged, favor ILD with possible fibrosis; infection unlikely. Recommend chest CT. No effusion or pneumothorax.
Increased pulmonary vascular congestion suggests borderline cardiac decompensation. Heart normal size; no pulmonary edema. Possible tiny bilateral pleural effusions. LLL opacity likely atelectasis.
Left pigtail catheter no longer seen; no pneumothorax. New left lateral opacity at prior catheter site-possible hemorrhage/contusion; follow-up advised. New epidural catheter; correlate. Unchanged.

No PTX, effusion, or new mediastinal widening. Chronic RML collapse, extrapleural fat, moderate cardiomegaly. Lungs clear, no edema. Pacemaker/ICD leads unchanged; prior LV lead replaced, new RA lead.
Stable heart/mediastinum. Right mid/lower opacities slightly improved; left mid/lower unchanged. Upper lungs clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Possible new lower-lobe fibrosis; CT advised.
Stable heart/mediastinum. Slightly improved right mid/lower opacities; left mid/lower unchanged. Upper lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Possible new lower-lobe fibrosis; consider CT.
Stable heart/mediastinum. Multifocal mid/lower-lobe peripheral/basal opacities. No effusion, pneumothorax, or edema. Differential: infection, COP, drug reaction. Chest CT recommended.
Low lung volumes; moderate scoliosis; retrocardiac lower-lobe opacity suggesting pneumonia; borderline cardiac size; mild descending aortic elongation; no effusion or edema.
No change from prior. Chest wall, hila, mediastinum, and lungs unremarkable; no pleural effusion. Borderline cardiac size; mild elongation of the descending aorta.
RUL pneumonia resolved. Central adenopathy slowly improving; enlarged right hilar & right lower paratracheal nodes. Repeat CXR in 3 months. Left lung clear. Heart normal size. No pleural abnormality.
Vs prior: right chest tube removed. Tiny right apical PTX and small right effusion persist. Left mod apical PTX unchanged; left basilar hydropneumothorax more evident. Bibasilar atelectasis improved.
Stable moderate L apical PTX with basilar loculated hydroPTX. R apical PTX resolved. R base subseg atelectasis. Resolving R chest subQ emphysema. No pulmonary edema. Subacute R rib 3,5,6 fx.
Increased bibasilar opacities likely developing pneumonia; recommend follow-up CXR in ___ weeks post-antibiotics. Stable biapical emphysematous changes. Results phoned to Dr. ___ at 11:15 on ___.
Severe cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular plethora, longstanding. Mild interstitial changes likely prior edema; no acute decompensation. No pleural effusion. Upper mediastinal widening (fat/venous).
PA/lateral chest: Persistent linear opacities in left lower lung near cardiac apex; no nodule. Lungs otherwise clear. Cardiomediastinal, hilar, pleural normal. Lower sternal pectus deformity.
Increased RUL and RML consolidation near sarcoid scarring, c/w acute pneumonia. F/u to exclude indolent infection or bronchial stricture. Central adenopathy stable. No effusion; heart normal.
Compared to prior, chronic moderate cardiomegaly improved. No pulmonary edema or vascular congestion. New tiny posterior pleural effusion (side indeterminate). RLL nodule regressing. No pneumonia.
New ill-defined retrocardiac left basal opacity with air bronchograms, favor pneumonia. No fibrosis/diffuse lung disease, pleural effusion or pulmonary edema. Mild cardiomegaly.
Right PICC: guidewire ends upper-mid SVC; catheter tip at CAJ. Lungs clear, heart normal size. Multiple healed rib fractures. Thin catheter likely VP shunt; tip not seen—correlate.
Increased right lower mediastinal contour suggests dilated gastric pull-up; possible atelectasis. Findings wax/wane on prior films. Consider pull-up obstruction, especially with recent vomiting.
Improved inspiration. Cardiac silhouette unchanged. Basal interstitial markings: congestion vs ILD; CT needed. Bibasilar atelectasis ± pleural fluid/thickening. RV apical pacer. No focal pneumonia.
S/p sternotomy. Very low lung vols with bilat mod effusions and bibasilar likely atelectasis; no edema. R apical nodules stable. Possible L loculated pleural fluid. No PTX. Aortic atherosclerosis.
Left basilar opacity, likely LLL - pneumonia/atelectasis/aspiration; possible loculated effusion (poorly defined). Mild-mod interstitial edema. PA/lateral after edema tx to reassess if indicated.
Stable cardiomegaly; prominent PA → pulm HTN (COPD); hyperinflation; coronary calcs; no effusion or PTX; small left diaphragmatic hernia; s/p RML wedge; DISH suspected; no new findings.
Mild interstitial pattern suggests vascular congestion; small loculated R pleural effusion; atelectasis likely but infection not excluded; posterior pigtail likely pleural, vs diaphragm uncertain.
Interstitial opacities resolved. Persistent moderate cardiomegaly. S/P right thoracentesis with small residual right effusion, partly subpulmonic; no left effusion or pneumothorax.
Stable heart/mediastinum. Interstitial changes improved. Partially loculated right pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Possible ILD. Emphysema better seen on recent CT.
Improved interstitial abnormality; possible atypical interstitial pneumonia or pulmonary edema with moderate–severe emphysema. If steroid-treated, NSIP. Heart normal; no adenopathy/pleural disease.
Possible peribronchial RLL infiltrate ?early infection, over ant costal calcs; chronicity unclear. Check prior CXR; if none, get obliques. Lungs otherwise clear; heart/mediastinum/hila/pleura normal.

Improved R basal atelectasis. Small subpulmonic R effusion persists. Lungs otherwise clear; no left pleural abnormality. Normal heart size. Neoesophagus moderately air-distended unchanged. No pneumothorax.
Stable RLL collapse with right pleural effusion. Decubitus views to distinguish atelectasis vs effusion. Lungs otherwise clear. Left lung nodule is nipple. Cardiomediastinum normal.
No pneumonia. Resolved prior right pleural effusion and pulmonary vascular congestion. 2.2×1.4 cm ovoid density left of upper trachea—possible calcified thyroid nodule; consider thyroid US.
No pneumothorax after R chest tube removal; small SC gas R upper abdomen. L base opacity decreased with clearer hemidiaphragm; retrocardiac opacity increased on lateral, possible consolidation.
New R juxtahilar opacity: likely early pneumonia; possible recurrence with enlarged/dense R hilum. Treat pneumonia; short-term CXR f/u. If aortic dissection concern, urgent chest CTA; CXR insensitive
Pulmonary fibrosis; no CHF signs. CT air trapping suggests chronic HP. RML/lingula opacities + RUL nodule: fibrosis vs infection. Follow-up CXR after antibiotics if needed; CT if nodule persists.
After right chest tube removal: stable postop changes; increased right subQ emphysema, possible air leak; f/u imaging advised. Left lung clear; cardiomediastinal unchanged; no large effusions.
Extensive subQ emphysema R chest wall/neck, now also L neck; unchanged. Tiny R apical pneumothorax suspected. Postop and cardiomediastinum stable. No edema, consolidation, or effusion.
Increasing subcutaneous emphysema suggesting air leak. Cardiomediastinal contours unchanged. No consolidation. Stable RUL postop changes. No large effusions. No pneumothorax; limited by emphysema.
Extensive subcutaneous emphysema R chest wall to bilateral neck, increased on L; possible air leak. No pneumothorax. s/p wedge resection. No pneumonia or edema; tiny R effusion/pleural thickening.
Lungs clear. Left hilar increased density with anterior shadow; possible perihilar nodule—recommend shallow+routine RAO views. No adenopathy; mediastinum/pleura normal. Incidental azygos fissure.
New/increased small R pleural effusion obscuring R base; possible small pneumonia or mass. Repeat CXR w/ oblique/decubitus in weeks; CT if needed. No L effusion. Chronic mild-mod cardiomegaly.
Heart size top-normal; mediastinum stable. Markedly improved parenchymal opacities, minimal. No effusion/pneumothorax. Suspected right lower lung nodules—consider dedicated chest CT; not on prior CT.
No acute lung process. T-spine: possible mild R convexity, minimal degeneration; rest unremarkable. No free air; no dilated upper bowel. L clavicular companion shadow not seen; r/o supraclav LAD.
Upper lungs clear. Lower lungs, esp left, underinflated; unchanged from prior intubated study. Indeterminate small pneumonia vs atelectasis. Heart top-normal; no vascular dilation/edema.

Post-resection L lung air slightly improved Large pleural space unchanged; more fluid. L neck/chest SQ emphysema slightly improved R lung clear Marked L mediastinal shift;L hemidiaphragm high persist.

R pigtail catheter present. Decreased R pleural effusion. R apical PTX decreased but persists small-mod. R basal opacity likely atelectasis, unlikely infection. L lung clear. Heart/mediastinum stable.
Compared to prior: right chest tube on water-seal. Right pneumothorax markedly increased. Small right basal air-fluid level better seen. Leftward cardiac shift suggests tension physiology.
Lungs clear. Chronic scarring near expansile lytic rib lesion, R ant 3–4. Stable mediastinal fat widening. No pleural effusion or central adenopathy. Heart normal. No active intrathoracic infection.
Lungs expanded and clear; no consolidation/effusion/adenopathy/infection. Heart size normal. Stable widened mediastinal fat. Chronic scarring adjacent to expansile lytic R ant 3rd–4th rib lesion.
Left pleural effusion markedly increased, occupying much of hemithorax; mild rightward cardiomediastinal shift; extensive LLL atelectasis. Right lung unchanged. Pacemaker and HD catheter in place.
Persistent right lower hemithorax opacity and elevated right hemidiaphragm with plate-like right basilar atelectasis; compatible with large right Morgagni hernia. If prior repair, CT advised.
Pulm vascular congestion resolved. RLL opacity nearly cleared (edema/atelectasis). LLL collapsed. Small B/L pleural effusions stable. Chronic mild cardiomegaly. No PTX. Trachea not assessable.
CXR: Small bilateral pleural effusions decreased. Lungs clear. Heart size normal. Aorta enlarged, no focal dilation. Sternal wires intact; misalignment stable since surgery. No pneumothorax.
CXR: Post sternotomy, AVR ± CABG. Normal heart size/vasculature. Unchanged mild chronic interstitial changes. No effusion or pneumonia. Stable aortic contour; heavy arch calcification to H&N origins.

Post sternotomy with AVR, possible CABG. Heart size/pulm vasc normal. Stable mild chronic interstitial change. No effusion/pneumonia. No aortic contour change. Calcified arch to head/neck vessel origins.

RIJ line tip mid-distal SVC. Post-CABG with stable postop contours. Small bilateral effusions; left basilar atelectasis. Improved lung volumes. No pulm edema/pneumothorax. Thoracic spine degeneration.
CXR: Increased small R pleural effusion. Greater RUL atelectasis with new/possible cavitation, favor post-radiation fibrosis. Assess for superinfection incl Aspergillus. L lung clear; heart normal.
Right apical primary lung mass increased. Right hilar fullness c/w lymphadenopathy. Increased R mid/upper retic opacities: postradiation fibrosis vs postradiation pneumonia. Chest CT recommended.
Since prior: decreased small R pleural effusion and R paratracheal fullness (improved mediastinal LAD). Fissural thickening persists; RLL atelectasis improved. Mild cardiomegaly unchanged. No edema.
Stable right apical pneumothorax without tension. Prior RLL opacity resolved; small right infrahilar atelectasis persists. Left lung unremarkable, heart size normal. No pneumonia or effusions.
Little change. Cardiomegaly post-CABG; no congestion; consider cardiomyopathy vs pericardial effusion. R pleural effusion decreased with minor fissure fluid; mild R base atelectasis. No pneumonia.
Tracheal narrowing with rightward deviation, stable vs prior CT. Obscured R heart border; no def consolidation; early pneumonia possible. Left hilar mass on prior CT; LLL mass better evaluated on CT.
New right PICC, tip in mid SVC, uncomplicated. Post-right thoracocentesis. No pneumothorax. Right pleural effusion slightly decreased. Heart and left lung unchanged.
Unchanged R hemidiaphragm eventration and L Bochdalek hernia. New small bilateral pleural effusions (R>L). No pneumonia/edema. Minimal biapical pleural thickening. New lower thoracic compression fx.
After bilat pigtail pleural drain removal: no pneumothorax. Stable mod-sev bibasilar atelectasis, minimal bilat effusions, elevated diaphragm, borderline cardiomegaly due to low volumes.
Chronic R hilar/subcarinal nodes; hilar ↑, CT stable. LLL peribronch opac ↑ with mild vol loss—progressed vs CT. Poss aspiration due subcarinal mass compressing esoph. R lung clear; heart nl; no CHF
Since prior: small R pleural effusion resolved; RUL postobstructive atelectasis/consolidation partly cleared; LLL platelike atelectasis slightly improved; thoracic LAD and R chest-wall mass unchanged

Compared to prior: L hemidiaphragm persistently elevated; LLL atelectasis improved. Stable RUL vol loss & R hilar adenopathy. Unchanged destructive R mid-rib lesion+ST mass. No PTX/effusion. Heart nl.
Moderately progressive lytic lesion at R 7th rib with large soft-tissue mass. No other rib lesions or VCF. Mild parenchymal fibrosis near R major fissure persists. No effusion. Normal heart size.
L pleural catheter removed since prior. Slightly increased L pleural effusion, prob subpulm with focal loculation. Cardiomediastinum stable. R lung: basilar linear atelectasis; mid-R surg sutures.
Persistent right pleural effusion. Unchanged right infrahilar cavity with air-fluid level, concerning for abscess. Worsened bilateral patchy opacities (likely infection); no pneumothorax. CT pending.
Interval right IJ Port-A-Cath with tip mid SVC; possible catheter looping at insertion. Free intraperitoneal gas post-op. Left basal opacity likely atelectasis; pneumonia not excluded.
No pneumothorax/effusion. Lungs clear; R-base subsegmental atelectasis. RV pacer/ICD leads. Asc aorta tortuous/dilated. Small hiatal hernia. Severe osteolysis of prox L humerus; correlate; x-rays.
CXR: Lungs clear/expanded. Severe sternal pectus (not cause of pain). Mediastinal/hilar normal; calcified aortic knob. Pleura normal. Mild thoracic scoliosis; osteophytes; no marked disc narrowing.

CXR: Lungs clear; severe pectus deformity (unlikely pain source); normal cardiomediastinal/hilar; calcified aortic knob; no pleural abn; mild T-spine scoliosis; multilevel osteophytes; mild disc narrowing.
Left lower lobe superior-segment consolidation c/w pneumonia. Right base opacity likely scar/atelectasis. Possible tiny left pleural effusion. Cardiomediastinal normal. No pneumothorax.
Right supraclavicular dialysis catheters to SVC-RA junction and mid RA. Possible thoracic inlet mass (chronic hematoma vs enlarged thyroid/parathyroid). Heart normal, lungs clear, no pleural disease.
Retrocardiac opacity increased, concerning for pneumonia. Change in cardiomediastinal contour with increased AP window opacity suggests pulmonary hypertension. Recommend ECHO, consider CT chest.
Previous lingular/lower-lobe opacities resolved. New LUL anterior opacity c/w pneumonia. New sub‑cm right lung nodule. Moderately severe emphysema. Normal heart size. No effusion or adenopathy.
No acute cardiopulm abnormality. 1 cm density at L humeral greater tuberosity - recommend L shoulder radiographs. Indistinct nodular opacity over R 5th rib; parenchymal/osseous/artifact - f/u CXR.
LLL atelectasis slightly improved; left effusion decreased. RLL atelectasis and right effusion stable. No pneumothorax or edema. Postop cardiomegaly unchanged. RIJ line tip in upper SVC.
Previously seen apical left pneumothorax has resolved. LUL collapse from bronchial valves with leftward mediastinal shift mimicking pneumothorax on lateral. Right lung and LLL clear. No effusion.
R basilar chest tube. Small bilat effusions. Tiny poss loculated hydroPTX at catheter tip; no large PTX. Stable RLL scar; L basal atelectasis/scar. No consolid/edema. T-spine DJD. No interval change.
Stable small R loculated basilar empyema with small R effusion. Unchanged patchy bibasilar opacities. No new consolidation, edema, or PTX. Cardiomediastinum stable. Mid-thoracic degenerative changes.
Previously seen right apical nodular opacity no longer visualized. Current CXR normal: no pneumonia, pulmonary edema, or pleural effusions. Cardiac silhouette normal in size.
Enlarged heart—cardiomegaly vs pericardial effusion. Lungs inflated; no consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. Retrosternal aeration adequate; consider CT if retrosternal mass suspected.
Left lung nodule real (not left nipple), less distinct; likely resolving. Repeat PA/lateral/oblique CXR in 2 wks; if persists, CT. Heart upper nl; lungs clear; no pleural abn; RA/RV leads in place.
Prior films: CHF resolved. No effusion/congestion; mild cardiomegaly persists. Left chest pacer with intact RA/RV leads. New LLL peribronchial opacity—favored atelectasis. Calcified aorta.
CHF resolved; no effusion or vascular congestion. Mild cardiomegaly persists. Dual-lead pacer from left chest. New LLL opacity—likely atelectasis vs early pneumonia. Calcified thoracic aorta.
Decreased pneumomediastinum with persistent left mediastinal fluid. Small right pleural effusion and mild–moderate basilar atelectasis persist. Chronic elevated right hemidiaphragm. No pneumothorax.
Right apical small irregular opacities and pleural margin irregularity, likely post-infectious. Compare with prior films; if unavailable, chest CT advised. No acute cardiopulmonary process.
Right apical small irregular opacities and pleural irregularity, likely post-infectious. Compare with prior films; if none, chest CT. No acute cardiopulmonary process. Findings phoned to provider.
Stable. Increased lung volumes. No pneumothorax at RUL wedge site. Borderline heart size; mild descending aortic elongation. No pneumonia/edema/effusion. Small platelike atelectasis on lateral only.
Unchanged. No acute cardiopulmonary disease. Hyperinflation c/w COPD. Persistent cardiomegaly. No vascular congestion, effusion, or pneumonia. Apical pleural changes c/w old TB.

Heart size normal. Stable R hilus likely dilated PA/calcified nodes; stable L basal opacity likely atelectasis; infection not excluded. Stable RML atelectasis. No effusion/pneumothorax. CT if warranted.
No significant change from prior. Low lung volumes; elevated left hemidiaphragm. Mild fluid overload; no overt edema. Parenchymal scarring mainly in RUL and LLL. No pneumothorax or effusions.
Borderline heart size. Possible mild hyperinflation (diaphragms not flattened). Right apical pneumothorax cannot be excluded; consider expiratory frontal view. No acute pulmonary process. Scoliosis.
Compared to prior, mild LA-predominant cardiomegaly decreased. Volumes improved; lungs clear. No pulmonary vascular abnormality, edema, effusion, pleural disease, or adenopathy. LUQ surgical clips.

Vs prior: decreased mild cardiomegaly, mainly left atrial. Lung volumes improved. Lungs clear. No vascular congestion, edema, effusion, pleural disease, or central adenopathy. Clips left upper abdomen.
Infrahilar nonspecific opacity on lateral CXR, possibly pulmonary venous confluence or obliquity artifact. Recommend repeat lateral; if persistent, proceed to chest CT.
Stable cardiomediastinal/hilar contours. No effusion, pneumothorax, or consolidation; lungs clear and well-expanded; pulmonary vasculature normal. Post-CABG and left dual-lead pacemaker (RA/RV).
Vs prior, fluid decreased in right pleural fluid/pneumothorax; still occupies unspecified % of right hemithorax. Left lower-lobe and right perihilar atelectasis. Left heart border unchanged.
RV pacer lead with long RA course to RV. Post-CABG sternotomy. Healed left posterolateral rib fractures. Mild cardiomegaly. Lungs clear. No pneumothorax, effusion, or mediastinal widening.
New bilateral peripheral interstitial opacities with apicobasal gradient and possible honeycombing, concern for ILD. No effusion, PTX, or mediastinal LAD. Chest CT recommended; infection less likely.
~10 cm homog, non-calcified, sharp left apical mass contacting chest wall/mediastinum/hilum/±aortic arch. Bilat solid nodules (largest 2 cm RUL) susp for mets. No PNA/effusion/edema; cardiac size nl.
↑ hyperinflation suggests more small-airway obstruction/worsening emphysema. No focal lung abnormality or effusion. Stable mild cardiomegaly. Large calcified thoracic aorta without focal dilation.

Chest X-ray: R apical calcified granuloma; minimal lingular scarring; no TB reactivation. Hyperinflation/flat diaphragms suggest emphysema or small airway obstruction. Heart, hila, mediastinum normal.
CXR: Mild interstitial changes with small bilat pleural effusions; heart normal; no vascular distention. Edema > infection. Repeat CXR after clearing for poss 8 mm L lung nodule.
Improved inspiration vs prior. Cardiac silhouette upper normal; mild aortic tortuosity. Mild left basilar atelectasis. No congestion, effusion, or pneumonia. Left IJ Port-A-Cath to mid-lower SVC.
New moderate right pleural effusion and moderate RLL consolidation obscuring prior small peripheral nodule. Favor infection involving pleura; infarct/malignancy less likely unless repeated PE.
Better inspiration vs prior. Cardiomegaly w/ mild pulm venous HTN. No acute pneumonia or vascular congestion. Apical scarring from old granulomatous disease. No radiographic amiodarone toxicity.
Lung volumes improved. Unchanged mild pulmonary edema with partially fibrosing interstitial disease. Basal opacities may reflect aspiration. No effusion. Heart top-normal; no vascular congestion.
No acute cardiopulmonary process. Marked right-convex lower thoracic scoliosis. Small right lower-lung lesion vs nipple shadow; repeat PA CXR with nipple markers.
LLL bronchiectasis; stable postop consolidation (likely atelectasis). New R peribronchial opacity; aspiration vs bronchiectasis flare. No edema. Tiny left pleural effusion. Heart normal.
No acute cardiopulmonary process or significant interval change. Prior CT peribronchovascular ground-glass opacities(L>R bases) and ≤3 mm nodules not well seen on CXR; may persist. CT more sensitive.
No acute cardiopulmonary process; no interval change. Prior CT showed L>R peribronchovascular GGOs not seen on radiograph and may persist. Pulmonary nodules ≤3 mm not well seen; CT better.
Vs prior: slight increase in peribronchial thickening/impaction in bibasilar bronchiectasis on lateral; frontal stable. Emphysema; hyperinflation. No edema/consolidation. Tiny maybe new R effusion.
Little recent change; progressive over years: enlarged ascending aorta, pulm vasc engorgement, chronic progressive ILD; prior edema resolved; enlarged hila suggest PAH. CT advised.
Residual right apical pneumothorax: minimal on frontal, small-moderate anterior on lateral. Lungs clear, no effusion. Heavy mitral annular calcification. Normal heart size. Fiducial markers noted.
Moderate right pneumothorax enlarging despite right pigtail drain; pleural air superior/lateral/anterior/basal. New small right effusion. Left lung clear. Heart size normal.
RUL 11 mm nodule, stable vs recent prior; was ≥17 mm on earlier scan. No other nodules. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion. New mild subsegmental atelectasis at right base, likely insignificant.
RUL 11 mm nodule unchanged since prior; previously >=17 mm on earlier exam. No other nodules. Heart normal size. No pleural effusion. New right basal subsegmental atelectasis, likely not significant.
Stable small-mod R apical PTX with R mediastinal shift; small bilat effusions (R posterior/subpulmonic) vs RML atelectasis. LLL cleared; possible early LUL consol. Heart nl. F/U; CT if needed.
Little change from prior. Healed left rib fractures; mild costophrenic angle obscuration, possibly pleural thickening. Retrocardiac atelectasis/fibrosis. No vascular congestion; right lung clear.
Small left pleural effusion and moderate LLL atelectasis, likely unchanged. No pneumothorax. RA/RV ICD leads in expected position. Heart size normal; no mediastinal widening. Right lung clear.
Small left pleural effusion and moderate LLL atelectasis, likely unchanged. No pneumothorax. Pacemaker leads appropriately positioned. Normal heart size, no mediastinal widening. Right lung clear.

R PICC unchanged; clips removed. R hemithorax decreased. Mild L chest wall thickening, slight prog. Small loculated L pleural effusion. Minimal L base scar/atelectasis. Heart & R lung unchanged normal
New left pectoral pacer; RA/RV leads in expected course. No PTX/effusion/mediastinal widening. Bilat upper-lobe fibrosis with traction bronchiectasis suggests sarcoidosis. No acute change.
vs prior: right lung volume increased; mild-moderate right pleural effusion with basal atelectasis persists. No pneumothorax. Normal heart. Retrocardiac atelectasis resolved. Left lung clear.
Little change vs prior. Right apical nodule unchanged. Increased left basal opacity c/w atelectasis and possible post-op hemidiaphragm tenting. Right lung clear; no vascular congestion.
Right chest tube removed. Minimal right chest wall subcutaneous emphysema; no pneumothorax. Low lung volumes; stable mild mediastinal widening. Bibasilar atelectasis likely. No large effusions/edema.
New large L pleural effusion; cardiomegaly with rightward displacement, trachea midline—likely pericardial effusion/pericarditis. LLL obscured: atelectasis vs consolidation. CT or post-thoracentesis.
No change. Lung vol nl. B/L apical thickening. Borderline heart size; mild aortic tort. Left pect pacer stable. No pulm mets/effusion/edema. Lateral retrocardiac hyperlucency c/w small hiatal hernia.
Left base/CPA opacity, likely atelectasis. No consolidation/nodule or PTX. 2 cm spinal opacity c/w vertebroplasty. Multiple wedge deformities/osteopenia. Calcified aorta. Normal heart size. No rib fx
No active/latent TB. Small linear lingular consolidation on lateral view; possible infection, inflammation, scar, or atelectasis. Patient asymptomatic; doctor notified. Recommend follow-up CXR.
Right subpulmonic pleural effusion increased; possible loculation vs pericardial eff. Right lat decub CXR suggested. Small left eff slightly increased. Upper abd large-bowel distention.
R pleural effusion increased (subpulmonic). Change in R heart border suggests medial loculation vs pericardial eff. R lateral decub CXR advised. Slightly larger L effusion. Dilated large-bowel loops.
Chest X-ray normal: lungs clear/expanded; normal cardiomediastinal, hilar, pleural surfaces. No radiographic intrathoracic malignancy. Vessels may mimic nodules; CT better for small nodules.

Decreasing bilateral pleural effusions and mild left basal atelectasis. No pneumothorax, edema or pneumonia. Small prevascular postoperative gas bubbles on lateral; cardiomediastinal silhouette normal.
Compared to prior, new anterior LLL opacity with air bronchograms and retrocardiac lucency loss, highly suggestive of pneumonia. No effusion/edema. Reactive left hemidiaphragm. Mild cardiomegaly.
Since prior: new small right pleural effusion; increased right basilar atelectasis. No edema or pneumothorax. Borderline cardiac size with mild descending aortic elongation. Left axillary clips.

Low lung vols; bibasilar atelectasis; mild pulm edema; no consolidation. Severe T12 compression deformity, age indeterminate; check tenderness. Possible inferior R shoulder subluxation; if pain/trauma.
CXR: Hyperinflation (emphysema/small-airways). Bilat nipple shadows at 5th ribs mimic nodules. Possible R lung nodule at scapula/3rd ant rib; oblique views. No effusion/adenopathy. Tortuous aorta
CXR: Hyperinflation (emphysema/small airway obstruction). Nipple shadows. Poss small R lung nodule at scapula/3rd ant rib—obliques. Clear; no effusion or adenopathy. Tortuous aorta; not dilated.

RML equivocal on frontal; likely normal. Lungs clear. No pleural or central LAD. Mildly widened upper mediastinum (?enlarged R thyroid vs tortuous vessels). Mild cardiomegaly improved. F/u CXR; CT PRN.
RML equivocal; lungs clear. No pleural or central adenopathy. Mild mediastinal widening, R thyroid enlargement vs tortuous vessels. Mild cardiomegaly, improved. Repeat CXR in ___ wks; consider CT.
AP chest: Left upper lobe lesion stable vs prior frontal view; this radiograph pair can serve as baseline for CXR follow-up, CT not required. No pleural effusion; lungs otherwise clear.
R chest wall air resolved. No pneumothorax. Unchanged R paramediastinal contour; postop? monitor. Min R pleural effusion (lateral only). R lung normal vol. No cardiomegaly. Mild tortuous desc aorta.
Probable COPD; cardiomegaly. Increased bibasilar opacities, likely atelectasis/scar; pneumonia not excluded. Upper-zone redistribution; no CHF. Thyroid enlargement displaces trachea right.
COPD with cardiomegaly. Bibasilar patchy opacities likely atelectasis/scar; infection not excluded. Likely mild pulmonary edema. Stable thyroid enlargement with rightward tracheal deviation.
PA/lateral: vs prior large LLL pneumonia, lungs clear/expanded. Cardiomediastinal/hilar/pleura normal; no chest wall abnormality. Subtle rib lesions not excluded; targeted views if focal.
Compared to prior CXRs: mild pulmonary edema resolved; no pneumonia. Severe cardiomegaly persists. Right lower paratracheal fullness likely distended azygos vein (per prior CTA). No pleural disease.
Normal heart and mediastinum. Left lung clear. Improved right lung base, but persistent pleural thickening with likely loculated effusion and adjacent atelectasis (anterior RML). No pneumothorax.
Right IJ line removed. Very small right apical pneumothorax. Bilateral pleural effusions. Bibasilar opacities likely partial lower-lobe atelectasis. Post-CABG changes stable. No pulmonary edema.
Decreased lung volumes. Platelike atelectasis at right hilum; minimal atelectasis at left lung bases. No pneumonia, edema, or pleural effusions. Heart size normal.
Since prior: extubated, NG tube removed. Normal lung volumes. Only subtle nonspecific parenchymal scarring; no pneumonia or edema. Cardiomediastinal and hila unremarkable.
Post-op RLL: small right effusion, pleural thickening, small right apical pneumothorax; improving right lung opacities; lateral pleural fluid accumulation. New LLL opacity worrisome for pneumonia.
Stable: localized air levels of known empyema. Left basal chest tube; no pneumothorax. Right lateral chest wall opacity unchanged. Left lung clear. Persistent cardiomegaly, no PV congestion.
Two right chest tubes. Improved aeration of left lung and RUL. Persistent RLL hazy infiltrate with dense consolidation/volume loss. Small bilateral effusions. No pneumothorax. Severe cardiomegaly.
Low lung volumes. Bilateral atelectasis/scar. Irregular L mid/lower opacities; ?peribronchial infiltrate/bronchiectasis. Heart normal. No effusion or central adenopathy. Get prior films; consider CT.
Possible lung opacity barely visible; upper-lobe asymmetry. Shallow oblique views with BB skin marker; disrobed, hair out; radiologist review. Lungs otherwise clear. Heart/hila/pleura normal.
Dual-chamber pacer with RA/RV apex leads unchanged. Cardiac silhouette less prominent (likely PA). No pulmonary edema or focal pneumonia. Blunted left costophrenic angle.
